About

I am an early-career physician-epidemiologist and Assistant Professor of Public Health at the Addis Continental Institute of Public Health (ACIPH) in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. My work spans clinical research and clinical trials, maternal, newborn and child health, nutrition, respiratory health and digital health.

After qualifying in medicine at Addis Ababa University, I practised as a general practitioner for four years, including frontline COVID-19 care, before completing a Master of Public Health and moving into research. I have since contributed to multi-site trials and implementation studies with partners including Jhpiego, the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, Brown University, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and University Medical Center Groningen, and I am a collaborator on the Global Burden of Disease Study.

My methodological strengths lie in the design, conduct and analysis of quantitative studies, including cluster randomized trials, longitudinal follow-up and multi-country surveys, complemented by qualitative and mixed methods. I teach epidemiology and biostatistics and supervise postgraduate research.

I am committed to generating rigorous evidence that informs clinical practice, public health policy and health system improvement, and I welcome collaboration with colleagues working on related questions.

    Antenatal and Postnatal Research Collective (ARC)

    ARC is a research collective testing new models to improve the quality and reach of antenatal, childbirth and postnatal care. As ACIPH’s research focal person, I contributed to three ARC studies in Ethiopia.

    Lead analyst and first author

    Evaluated a six-meeting group antenatal care model, facilitated by health extension workers at health posts in the Amhara region, designed to increase antenatal care attendance and facility delivery.

    My responsibilities

    • Led the quantitative analysis of the cluster randomized evaluation.
    • Led the qualitative pilot study, from analysis to publication.
    • Managed study data and reporting for ACIPH.

    Key findings

    The pilot showed that group antenatal care can feasibly be introduced at health-post level: enough pregnant women of similar gestational age were identified to form groups, and women were willing to keep attending.

    Outputs Pilot and Feasibility Studies, 2026 Equity analysis, medRxiv preprint, 2025 Best Oral Abstract in Public Health, ISCOMS 2025

    Co-Investigator

    Tested a self-care model in Ada’a District in which mothers, supported by their families and a home-care kit, carry out daily health checks on themselves and their newborns during the first week after birth.

    My responsibilities

    • Co-investigator on the study team.
    • Contributed to interpreting results and writing both study publications.

    Key findings

    Postnatal checks between 24 and 72 hours after birth rose from 9% of mothers before the intervention to 96% after it. Families and health workers found the model feasible and acceptable; all health centres continued it, and 97% of home-care kits still worked six months after project support ended.

    Outputs PLOS Global Public Health, 2026 BMJ Public Health, 2026

    Co-Investigator

    A cluster randomized trial in Ethiopia, Kenya and Nigeria testing a package of interventions to help women have a companion of their choice during labour, birth and after birth in health facilities.

    My responsibilities

    • Co-investigator on the study team.
    • Qualitative data analysis for the Ethiopian study sites.

    Key findings

    In Ethiopia, after 12 months, 87% of births in intervention facilities had a continuous birth companion, compared with none in control facilities (preprint).

    Outputs medRxiv preprint, 2025

    Antenatal Balanced Energy-Protein (BEP) Targeting Strategies Study

    A trial evaluating strategies for deciding which pregnant women should receive balanced energy-protein supplements, aiming to improve birth outcomes, with follow-up of children to 12 months to assess growth and development.

    My responsibilities

    • On-site supervision and field implementation of the trial and its 12-month follow-up, coordinating 32 study nurses across nine health centres and three hospitals.
    • Daily data monitoring, quality assurance and weekly reporting.
    • Developing the analysis plan for the child growth and development follow-up.

    Status

    Ongoing. Findings will be shared here once published.

    EMECHAT: Postnatal Maternal Micronutrient Supplementation to Enhance Child Health and Thriving

    A randomized trial testing whether giving mothers multiple micronutrient supplements after birth improves breast-milk micronutrients and infant brain development.

    My responsibilities

    • Participant safety and clinical care, including assessment and reporting of adverse events.
    • Coordination of field activities at study health facilities.

    Digital Health Readiness among People with COPD in Europe

    An analysis of survey data from 232 people living with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, identifying groups of patients according to their intention to use digital health interventions.

    My responsibilities

    • Data preparation, cluster analysis and validation.
    • Interpretation and manuscript writing.
    • Presented the work during my 2026 fellowship at UMCG.

    Key findings

    Two distinct patient groups emerged. In the larger group, 84% intended to use digital health, and across both groups the perceived usefulness of the tools predicted intention to use them.

    Outputs Healthcare, 2026

    Ongoing

    Text-Message Reminders for Diabetes Medication Adherence

    A hospital-based study of adults living with diabetes assessing their intention to use SMS reminders to support medication adherence, and the factors associated with it.

    My responsibilities

    • Led the study and manuscript as first author.
    • Presented at CPHIA 2023, Lusaka, with an Africa CDC scholarship.

    Key findings

    Two-thirds (66%) of 333 respondents intended to use SMS reminders, pointing to strong potential for text-message support in diabetes care.

    Outputs PeerJ, 2024
    2025 – present
    Ongoing

    Global Burden of Disease (GBD) Study

    The GBD Study produces comprehensive estimates of health loss from diseases, injuries and risk factors across 204 countries and territories. As a member of the collaborator network, I contribute to GBD 2023 analyses, including the global burden of cervical cancer and of type 1 diabetes.
